Subject: NorthBank private deploy - cluster sizing & segmentation questions

Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As we start lining up procurement and rack allocation, a few items came up from our infrastructure team that will affect the node pool and storage decisions: 

- We have three distinct failure domains in our colo (A/B/C) with separate power and fabric. Can your on-prem package map node pools to failure domains and prefer anti-affinity between pools?
- We want a small GPU pool for inference (up to 8 GPUs), a mixed pool for model compilation and light batching, and a large CPU-only pool for system components and batch jobs. Hoping to keep cost predictable.
- Disk type: NVMe for model cache, but we need guidance on PV sizing and eviction strategy for KV caches (what's safe to evict vs persisted storage).
- Can Redwood's Private control plane run in a single failover replica across zones or do you recommend 3 replicas in a quorum?

I've attached our current cluster requirements (cluster-requirements-v1.pdf) and a quick topology sketch. Can you route this to the right technical folks and propose a short checklist we can use when we spin up the cluster?

Thanks,
Rajiv
Director, Platform Engineering
NorthBank Financial

Subject: Re: NorthBank private deploy - nodepool affinity and failure domains

Rajiv, Marissa —

I've put together a baseline node-pool and storage proposal after reviewing the requirements. High-level summary first, then details.

Summary:
- Control plane: 3 replicas (etcd quorum) running on dedicated control nodes isolated from workloads. Use anti-affinity across failure domains so leader election survives a single domain outage.
- Node pools:
  * inference-gpu: 8x A100-equivalent nodes (can be reduced to 4 for initial POC). Dedicated NVMe local scratch for ephemeral KV cache (500GB per node recommended), mount as ephemeralVolume + hostPath eviction policy.
  * compile-mix: 4x mixed nodes (GPUs optional), more RAM (256GB) for compilation jobs; small local SSD for temp artifacts.
  * system-batch-cpu: 6x CPU nodes with larger persistent volumes (Ceph/Rook-backed PVs) for system components, long-running jobs and stable model artifacts.
- Storage:
  * Model artifacts and long-term storage: replicated block storage (Rook Ceph) with 3x replication across failure domains. Use PVs sized by model catalog (start with 2TB pool).
  * KV/embedding cache: NVMe local for hot cache; treat as ephemeral (no persistence required) and rely on our automatic warm-up + prefetch on pod restart.
  * Backups: periodic object-store snapshots to S3-compatible bucket in a different network domain.
- Affinity and failure domains: label nodes with failure-domain=<A|B|C>. Use podAntiAffinity for control plane and preferredDuringScheduling for inference pods to distribute load. For strict locality (e.g., NVMe-backed pods) use nodeAffinity requiredDuringScheduling to pin to matching nodes.
- Network:
  * Private control plane to have outbound-only egress to Redwood-managed endpoints for license and health pings; an optional site-to-site VPN for telemetry.
  * Firewall: open ports for kubelet (10250), API (6443) only from management subnet; allow cluster-internal overlay (we recommend Calico in BGP mode).

Eviction guidance:
- KV cache eviction is safe; treat local NVMe as cache with size targets. Use evictionPriority annotations for pods that can be terminated first (batch/compile). Reserve at least 1 NVMe device per GPU node for model artifacts required for cold start.

Action items I will deliver by EOD Monday:
- Concrete sizing table (node CPU/GPU/disk) in CSV
- Example k8s manifests for node labels/taints/affinity
- Short checklist for control-plane HA and etcd snapshot cadence

Questions:
1) For the inference pool, do you require GPU passthrough for single-tenant workloads, or is multi-tenant acceptable for initial rollout?
2) Do you have a preferred object-storage for backups on-site (MinIO / S3 compatible)?

-Dev
